author: rcmacf
text:
Yep, you've got just about every FTR in there. The term "FTR" can be applied to pretty much every swing high in a downtrend (for example). If you can find the key FTRs, those where price has broken something significant prior to forming the FTR, those are the places to look to take trades from the "tip" of the FTR.

I've chosen not to draw in every FTR on this chart, but only those where price has broken something significant (the black lines showing previous lows). At these line, price has the choice to go up, or keep dropping. This gives them their significance -they are previous decision points. In each case, price breaks them, and it's very last effort to go higher is the tip of the FTR. I just roughly marked these in yellow. Each of these area will have significant points of supply in them, and we look to trade down from these, based on price action in a lower time frame.

I like the 3rd one down, it has broken 2 significant levels (the second, more minor level, is not marked in. It's about 1.0932)

author: joema
text:
Hi all just some input on deciphering direction and FLAG, FLAG LIMITS, FTR, BASE or RBD,DBR in my studies I continued to read what was in front of me continually forgetting to look left and on HTF and often getting confused on the why not here what about there and is it a FO or ENG. so here is an example of how I mark a chart to begin my reading of where we are going and where we are coming from on HTF so there is no confusion on direction and seeing FO's HTF base 1 is formed we can see in this base a weakening of bullish activity clearly.

The base is broken and a FLAG created which I marked FTR 1 the yellow horizontal lines that the box is made of represent the FLAG limits this is also as I marked an FTR. price then drops fast. slows and creates a HTF base 2 where we see what looks like CP then shoots up out of the box and creates FTR 2 which is the same principle as FTR 1. once FTR 2 was created we now have price in a range or FLAG between 2 FTR's we know that unless there is a break of one of them price will remain in between them and often an engulf of an FTR followed by a FO. if I was swing trading I would look to trade from FTR to FTR. if I was to take short term moves I will know why on the 1 hour why price engulfed a high only to reverse quickly or vice versa. naturally if scalping dropping down to an H4 or H1 and doing the same as this would be more helpful but always knowing whats up on HTF such as weekly and down will keep you out of trouble and guessing. there is no qaos in the market just trickery with rules. FLAGs are how the market is tracked

Ifmyante wrote: It's always best to be aware of which currency is going to cause the turn

If you want to, say, sell GU, you should know whether it's because of the dollar getting ready to rise, or the pound to fall Looking at the dollar pairs will tell you if it's the former, in which case you'll look for the pair with the best setup and room to move

If not, look at the various pound pairs, and if GBP is in Supply all round, you'll know that the turn will be due to oncoming pound weakness, making it the ideal time to sell

In essence, always be aware of who is about to turn the market

This will definitely help with knowing which currency is going to turn price.(Currency Futures)
